indicators.note: seed broadcast is scattered widely, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Asks whether a tin can could transmit some lark over the airwaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' scatters CANIT into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: An antic is a playful caper or prank, the same idea as a frolic.

clue.text: I've acted on new indication of a deal

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh version, so these letters are rearranged afresh

explanation.surface: Someone says they have acted on a new sign that a deal is coming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges IVEACTEDON. An advice note is a commercial document telling a buyer that goods have been sent.
explanation.definitionFit: This trade document notifies a customer of a dispatch, signalling a transaction has been carried out.

definitions.meaning: to produce or put out goods or printed copies
the verb sense: comes about, proves in the end to be

explanation.walkthrough: Read 'results' as a verb: things that turn out are things that result.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to produce output and to end up a certain way.

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so the remaining letters are reassembled
made shorter means the word certainly loses its final letter

explanation.surface: An instrument that has broken certainly ends up shorter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shorter' cuts the Y from CERTAINLY, leaving CERTAINL, which 'broken' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The clarinet is a woodwind musical instrument with a single reed.

clue.text: Mother has to think deeply about perfume holder

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the musing word wraps around the parent

parts.note: to ponder is to think deeply
Ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: Mother has to deliberate over which scent container to choose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' means around; 'has to' is only a link. A pomander was once carried to ward off bad smells.
explanation.definitionFit: A pomander is a ball or perforated case holding aromatic substances to scent a room or clothes.

definitions.meaning: a light slip-on shoe, such as for dancing or a court shoe
a device for drawing water from a well

explanation.walkthrough: 'well-used' reads as 'much worn', fitting shoes, but it means used at a well.
explanation.definitionFit: A light dancing shoe and a water-raising device share this single word.

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, and AB (able seaman) is a sailor too

indicators.note: wrong means set out incorrectly, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A man called Jack, told the wrong date, felt let down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' turns DATE into ATED. Jack and AB both mean a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Abated means reduced or diminished, as a storm or noise lessens.

definitions.meaning: St George, England's patron saint, slew a fire-breathing beast in legend
read as two words: to go on tediously and so bore

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as DRAG ON, which is what a bore does; the question mark flags the split.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend has Saint George fight and kill a monstrous winged serpent, his great adversary.

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the race word

parts.note: a run is a race
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A competitor in a race heads for disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts I inside RUN.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruin is a state of complete wreckage or collapse, the same as devastation.

clue.text: Using exactly the same words in Latin

definitions.text: Using exactly the same words in Latin

parts.words: Using exactly the same words in Latin
parts.note: the word for word-for-word quotation is itself borrowed directly from Latin

explanation.walkthrough: The clue defines the word and then notes that it is a Latin word itself.
explanation.definitionFit: This adverb means word for word, exactly as originally spoken or written, from medieval Latin.

parts.note: to pen is to write
a tag is a familiar quotation or saying
taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions to inscribe a quotation upon army headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: A tag is a stock quotation, often Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: The five-sided building in Virginia is the headquarters of the US Department of Defense.

clue.text: He may pass on what he knows

definitions.text: He may pass on what he knows

parts.words: He may pass on what he knows
parts.note: sounds like a teacher passing on knowledge, but means a candidate who passes a test on the strength of his knowledge

explanation.walkthrough: 'pass on' reads as 'hand down'; it means 'pass, by means of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sitting a test succeeds or fails according to what he has learned.

clue.text: In auditions, this vote will decide the issue

definitions.meaning: the choosing of actors for parts, which auditions serve

definitions.text: this vote will decide the issue
definitions.meaning: the deciding vote held by a chair when votes are tied

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is completed by 'vote': a chair's tie-breaking vote.
explanation.definitionFit: Selecting performers for roles is the process auditions belong to; a chairman's tie-breaker bears the same name.

parts.note: a gain is a profit
said means declared

explanation.surface: A company announced a profit, but the figure was challenged.
explanation.definitionFit: To gainsay is to deny or contradict, so a gainsaid claim was contested.

clue.text: Performed in a group that's dissolute

indicators.note: in places the carried-out word inside the group word

parts.note: a band is a group, especially of musicians
done means performed or carried out

explanation.surface: Someone played with a group of wild-living musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal, wrapping the group round the performed word, with A taken as written in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandoned can describe wanton, unrestrained behaviour, like dissolute living.

definitions.meaning: the military sense: a small party of troops assigned to a special task

explanation.walkthrough: 'detail' is not small particulars but soldiers sent on a duty.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both emotional aloofness and a unit of troops sent off on a task.

clue.text: Arresting society girl — given time, one should be repaid

parts.note: striking or remarkable
a deb is a debutante, a young woman entering high society

explanation.surface: A striking debutante, given enough time, ought to settle what she owes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arresting' sounds like police work but means striking.
explanation.definitionFit: Money owed and not yet settled is a liability awaiting repayment.
The phrasal verb covers both quitting a habit and yielding to an opponent.

indicators.note: in places the advertisement inside the fleeing word

parts.note: flight as running away is an escape
an ad is a notice or advertisement

explanation.surface: Watch, high in the air, for a songbird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' and 'lark' suggest birds; flight here is fleeing, and lark is a spree. 'in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapade is a daring or mischievous adventure, a bit of fun.

parts.note: reads as costing nothing, but means to clear someone of an accusation

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase for gratis is read as a verb: release from a criminal charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear a defendant of blame officially is to acquit or absolve them.

clue.text: Choir's made a mess of number — blooming thing

indicators.note: messing something up throws its letters into disorder

parts.note: the possessive 's adds no letter, so the group of singers gives its own five letters
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

explanation.surface: The singers botched a song, a real wretched effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made a mess of' rearranges CHOIR into ORCHI; 'number' is the Roman numeral D.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchid is a flowering plant, so a thing that blooms.

parts.note: reads as unite, but means sign up with the armed forces

explanation.walkthrough: 'forces' means the army, navy and air force.
explanation.definitionFit: Signing up for military service is joining the armed forces.

clue.text: Grave words for those who are late

definitions.text: Grave words for those who are late

parts.words: Grave words for those who are late
parts.note: serious words for latecomers, really an inscription on a tomb for the dead

explanation.walkthrough: 'Grave' means a burial place and 'late' means deceased.
explanation.definitionFit: This inscription on a tombstone commemorates the deceased.

parts.note: sounds like a small amount of joy, but means the sword-tap that confers knighthood

explanation.walkthrough: The ceremonial tap on the shoulder when knighting someone raises them in rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally the embrace or sword touch conferring knighthood; now any honour or praise.

indicators.note: rear as in the back end, so the word is read from back to front in this down entry

parts.note: a skua is a predatory seabird

explanation.surface: A bird has to raise the young of other birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'others' means other birds: SKUA turned round gives a different set of seabirds.
explanation.definitionFit: Auks are seabirds, so different birds from the skua in the wordplay.

clue.text: One of the Great Lakes up-country?

indicators.note: up in a down entry means the word is written upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland

explanation.surface: Asks whether one of the Great Lakes lies upcountry, inland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up-country' looks like one word meaning inland; split it into 'up' and 'country'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Erie is one of the five Great Lakes of North America.

parts.note: rough means hard or harsh
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A difficult period getting enough fibre in one's diet.
explanation.definitionFit: Roughage is the indigestible plant material in food that aids digestion.

clue.text: Points to case for a drug

parts.note: S and E are compass points, south and east
the dative is a grammatical case

explanation.surface: Someone indicates a medicine bottle and prescribes a drug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' is a grammatical case, not a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedative is a calming medicine that induces sleep or relaxation.

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are knocked out of their order

explanation.surface: A cricketer jumped out of the batting crease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges LEAPT. In cricket the crease is the line where the batsman stands.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleat is a fold pressed into cloth, a deliberate crease.
